components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. The value is normalized before
            it is stored and returned: surrounding whitespace is trimmed and
            internal runs of whitespace collapsed to a single space, it is
            upper-cased, and common street-type abbreviations are expanded as
            whole words (ST->STREET, RD->ROAD, AVE->AVENUE), e.g. '  12  main
            st ' is stored as '12 MAIN STREET'. An address that is blank after
            normalization is rejected.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
          x-field-extra-annotation: |-
            @jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank
            @org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.AddressValidation
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. The value is normalized to
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; an explicit
            leading '+' and country code are kept, otherwise country code '+61'
            is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the national
            digits. The result must have 8 to 15 digits after the '+' and is
            stored and returned in that canonical form (e.g. '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '0412 345 678'
          x-field-extra-annotation: |-
            @jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank
            @org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.TelephoneValidation
        email:
          title: Email
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional, but when present it
            must be a syntactically valid address; the value is stored and
            returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.Email"
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            When true, allow creating this owner even if another owner already
            has the same lastName and address (normally rejected with 409
            Conflict as a duplicate household). Write-only request flag; it is
            not persisted or returned.
          type: boolean
          writeOnly: true
          default: false
          example: false

              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.

            customerCode:

              description: >-

            householdId:

              type: string
              example: 'a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890'
              readOnly: true
            pets:

              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:

          required:

## Summary

I implemented the `namesakeCount` feature for owner creation in this Spring Boot PetClinic REST app. When an owner is created, the response (and subsequent GETs) now reports how many existing owners already shared the same `firstName` + `lastName` (case-insensitively) *before* this create.

Changes made:

1. **`ClinicServiceImpl.saveOwner`** — for new owners, computes `namesakeCount` via a new `countNamesakes` helper that counts existing owners matching first+last name case-insensitively (`equalsIgnoreCase`), run before the new owner is persisted so it isn't counted itself.

2. **`model/Owner.java`** — added a persisted `Integer namesakeCount` field (`@Column(name = "namesake_count")`) with getter/setter, following the same pattern as `householdId`/`customerCode`.

3. **`openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `namesakeCount` (int32, min 0) property to the `Owner` schema, so the generated `OwnerDto` carries it and MapStruct maps it automatically by name.

4. **DB schemas** — added a `namesake_count` column to the `owners` table in all four schema files (hsqldb, h2, mysql, postgres).

The acceptance test `coreCountsNamesakes` passes: the second owner sharing the name returns `namesakeCount = 1`. Full suite: **Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0**.

Note: the two owners in the test use different addresses, so they don't trigger the existing household-duplicate (409) rule; the extra `postcode` field in the payload is harmless since Jackson 3 ignores unknown properties by default.
